To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) epileptogenesis is the result of the reorganisation of neural circuits; (b) the excitotoxic cascade is a common pathway for neuronal death in epilepsia and cerebral ischemia; (c) apoptosis and necrosis are the main forms of neuronal death; (d) apoptosis is the result of activation of caspases and is inhibited by the caspase inhibitors; (e) necrosis is the result of calcium overload, and is prevented by calcium channel antagonists and

the mechanisms of neuronal death are similar in epilepsy and ischemia, that the excitotoxic cascade can be blocked by neuroprotective substances and that the mechanisms of epileptogenesis are similar to those of ischemic brain injury.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of the excitotoxic cascade and with the development of new neuroprotective agents.

the mechanisms of neuronal death, the role of free radical scavengers in the protection against neuronal death and with the role of CDP-choline in the protection against excitotoxic damage of the brain.

the elucidation of mechanisms of epileptic seizures, the development of new antiepileptic drugs, the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of neuronal death, and the search for neuroprotective substances.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the treatment of epilepsias should be based not only on the control of seizures but on the prevention of neuronal death as well.
epilepsy is not a disease, but a syndrome, and that the treatment of epilepsias is a matter of the individual patient and not of the disease.
the mechanisms of neuronal death in epilepsia are similar to those of the "excitotoxic cascade" in cerebral ischemia, and that the same substances may be used as neuroprotectants in epilepsias.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mechanisms of neuronal death are similar to those of ischemia and that the neuroprotection is also similar.
the excitotoxic cascade is initiated by a seizure and that the effector side is similar to the "ischemie cascade" which leads to neuronal death.
the epileptic seizure may be a cause or a consequence of neuronal death.
The main takeaway from our work is that
epilepsy may be a disease of the brain which is not necessarily incurable.
the excitotoxic cascade is the main mechanism of epileptogenicity, while the ischemic cascade may play a significant role in the pathogenesis of epilepsia in the case of secondary epilepsy.
the excitotoxicity cascade and the ischemic cascade are very similar and that the same substances may protect neurons from the effects of both.
